title: Keep DTOs pure immutable data

facts.note: Bun project source files (.ts/.tsx) by extension.
Excludes test files and vendored/build directories, which are never scanned; files with no layer segment are outside the rule.
Observer must detect that a scanned file declares a type/interface whose name ends in `DTO`, whether or not the current diff touches it; existing impure DTOs remain in scope.
Diff-level observer for the common trigger (DTO added or its members changed); not a prerequisite — any in-scope DTO must be pure.
Detector finding: method member or non-readonly field in any scanned `*DTO` declaration, including pre-existing ones.

fires: A coder adds or edits a `*DTO` type or interface in a layered non-test source file of a Bun project.
A task adds a field to an existing `*DTO` to carry data across a boundary.
A scanned layered file already contains a `*DTO` with a method or mutable field, even if the current change did not touch it.
The detector reports a method member or non-readonly field on any `*DTO` declaration.
doesNotFire: The `*DTO` declaration lives in a test file or in a vendored/build directory.
The file carries no layer segment in its path.
The scanned files contain no type or interface named `*DTO` at all.

given: a `*DTO` type or interface — the shape crossing a boundary — in a layered, non-test source file
when: that DTO is declared, changed, or present in any scanned file (including pre-existing declarations)
then: the DTO MUST have no method members and every field MUST be `readonly`.
prefer: Keep DTOs as immutable data: readonly fields only, no methods.
Put behavior in the layer that consumes or produces the DTO.
During GREEN: add only the readonly data fields the current boundary behavior requires.
During GREEN: reuse existing functions for transformation or behavior when available; add a small free function only when the current acceptance needs it.
avoid: Attaching convenience methods to the DTO.
Making fields mutable to simplify implementation.
why: A method on a DTO means behaviour crossed the boundary too, coupling both sides to an implementation rather than data; a mutable field lets the receiver change what the sender said. Both look harmless in one file and become impossible to unpick once a second consumer exists.
evidence: bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no method member or non-readonly field on any `*DTO` declaration in scanned files.
The affected DTO remains pure immutable data (all fields readonly, no methods).
verifier_detail: Detector parses each `*DTO` type/interface declaration body, splits its members on `;`, newline, or `,`, and flags any method member or any field lacking `readonly`.
Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.
audit: terms: dto = a `*DTO` type or interface — the shape crossing a boundary; pure_data = no method members, every field readonly.

sharedNodes.text: strict: the checker fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Activation facts, fires/doesNotFire scenarios derived from the DTO definition, the detector's whole-file scanning, and the scanning exceptions.
additions.justification: Required by the target structure; derived from source exceptions and terms, no new obligation.

Phase qualifier kept explicitly as 'During GREEN:' prefix.
Detector-wide exception; kept for the verifier.
